newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Stadium to redesign for Australian Rules.
newsitem.headline: Stadium to redesign for Australian Rules.

text.p: Olympic stadium owner-operator Stadium Australia Group said on Thursday the Australian Football League (AFL) would loan Stadium up to A$1 million to make design modifications to allow the stadium to be used for Australian Rules football after the 2000 Olympic games.

"The AFL has moved quickly and decided to take advantage of the window of opportunity which exists right now to ensure the stadium's design may accomodate AFL matches after the Olympics," AFL chief executive Wayne Jackson said in a statement, adding that there may be further expansion of the code in New South Wales in the future.

"If as expected there are five to six million people in the Sydney catchment area by the turn of the century, and support for the Sydney Football Club continues to grow, strong consideration will be given to a second AFL team in Sydney," Jackson said.
The loan is expected to be repaid from revenues derived from AFL matches held at the Stadium after the Olympics.
The News South Wales state government has also agreed in principle to contribute funding of up to A$700,000 to cover the balance of the verified construction costs.
